title: An SSH auth refusal during a network flap is classified, not an unclassified stop
description: epic-yoh, 2026-09-24 14:34 UTC: during a burst of network trouble (DNS failures minutes earlier), one git fetch of dyo's attempt branch got 'git@github.com: Permission denied (publickey)'. The same fetch succeeded a minute later with nothing changed. The run treated it as 'a stop this run has no classification for' and halted for a person. Classify git auth refusals: retry once or twice within the remote-transient bound, then refuse with a named class (remote_auth_refused) that says what to check (ssh-agent, key, deploy access). Never an unclassified stop.
acceptance_criteria: A git auth refusal is retried within the transient bound and, if it persists, refused as its own named class with remediation text; a test injects a one-off publickey refusal and the run continues
